title: Synthesis of failed rollout root causes, mitigations, and runbook hardening
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket captures the consolidated learnings from the recent failed model rollout (canary -> staged -> partial rollback), creates specific mitigations, and tracks runbook hardening and automation work. The goal is to ensure future canary/A-B/shadow deployments surface regressions earlier and either self-mitigate or fail safely before impacting production traffic.
timeline: 2026-02-09: Canary rollout started for model v2026-02-09-quant - 5% traffic in us-west1
2026-02-10 02:12 UTC: Elevated tail latency observed on the canary model via latency_p50/p95/p99 dashboards
2026-02-10 02:15 UTC: Error rate spike on tokenization stage for requests with long system prompts (>= 1024 tokens), service returned 500s
2026-02-10 02:25 UTC: Automated canary health check failed (p99 latency > 2.5s for 5m), auto-rollback did not trigger due to misconfigured signal mapping
2026-02-10 03:00 UTC: Manual rollback initiated, canary traffic returned to baseline model; incident declared; on-call paged

rca_summary: Three contributing issues were identified: 1) Tokenizer regression in the new model variant causing unhandled exceptions for long system prompts; 2) KV-cache eviction and batching interaction exposing a race under mixed batch-size traffic leading to increased latency and transient errors; 3) Canary signal mapping mistake where the health-check rule used p95 over 1m instead of p99 over 5m, so the auto-rollback policy did not evaluate the correct alarm and never triggered automatically.
mitigations: Patch tokenizer to handle long system prompts and release model v2026-03-12-fix-tokenizer
Introduce a protective input validation layer in the serving API to reject or truncate out-of-spec system prompts with a clear 4xx response and metric emission
Adjust KV-cache eviction policy to be batch-size aware; add locking around cache updates for mixed-batch scenarios
Change canary health signal to p99 over 5m for latency and a combined error-rate + 5xx spike detector; ensure thresholds are environment-specific
Temporarily tighten canary traffic caps for models with unknown tokenizer compatibility to 1% and enable shadowing for higher-volume validation
runbook_updates: Add pre-rollout checklist item: run full tokenizer compatibility test suite with representative prompt corpus (including >1024 token system prompts)
Update auto-rollback configuration docs: explain metric mappings, evaluation window defaults, and safe defaults to apply for all canaries
Create step-by-step play for manual mitigation when cache/batching anomalies occur: identify offending batch sizes, revert runtime config, and evict suspect cache shards
Include a 'shadow validation gate' step: require 24h of shadow traffic with automated mismatch detection before promoting to >1% canary
Document communication plan for rollbacks: stakeholders to notify, SLA updates, and external customer messaging template
telemetry_changes: Emit tokenizer-exception metric with labels for prompt_length_bucket and model_variant
Split latency histograms by batch_size and route (canary vs control) to detect mixed-batch regressions
Add synthetic canary traffic producer that runs end-to-end validation every 30m and posts results to a dedicated dashboard
Instrument KV-cache metrics for eviction_reason and concurrency_wait_time
Alerting: add composite alert that fires when (p99 latency > threshold AND error_rate increase > X) for 5m
rollout_config_changes: Default canary traffic limit reduced from 5% to 1% for new model variants unless an explicit waiver is granted
Enable mandatory shadowing for 48h for models with tokenizer changes or quantization changes
Require a signed-off rollout plan in the console with required telemetry queries and expected baselines before permitting staged promotion
Add automatic rollback hysteresis: if rollback fails due to control-plane errors, force circuit-breaker to stop promotion and page SRE

notes: Aim for automation-first mitigations where possible: better telemetry + correct signal mapping should have auto-rolled this canary back.
Avoid overly aggressive thresholds that create noisy rollbacks; use composite signals combining latency + errors.
Plan to run a cross-team rollout drill in Cycle 42 to validate the new runbook and auto-rollback behavior before the next larger release.
Keep knobs in the console for temporary emergency caps that SRE can toggle without a full release.
